scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that experts are better informed while arguing the public must have a say; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Modern problems are often so complex that ordinary people cannot study every detail.
One claim holds that major policy decisions should always be left to politicians and experts, on the reason that they are more informed and have better judgment than the public.
I agree that experts have valuable knowledge, but I disagree that major decisions should always be left to them alone.
First, there is real truth in the reason that experts are better informed.
Politicians and specialists often spend years studying the issues that ordinary citizens cannot.
For example, an economist may understand the likely effects of a tax far better than the average voter.
This shows that expert knowledge can lead to wiser and more careful decisions.
On highly technical matters, the advice of experts is genuinely valuable.
Leaving every detail to an uninformed public could produce hasty and harmful choices.
To this extent, the reason behind the claim has genuine force.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the public must have a say

sentences.text: Second, however, major decisions should not always be left to experts alone.
Big policies affect everyone, so the people who must live with them deserve a voice.
Consider a major decision about going to war, which changes countless lives and belongs to the whole nation.
Such matters show that values and priorities, not just expertise, should guide major choices.
Experts can also be mistaken, biased, or focused too narrowly on their own field.
A government that ignores the public entirely soon loses both trust and legitimacy.
Major decisions, then, need the knowledge of experts and the consent of the people.
In conclusion, experts truly are better informed on many complex issues.
But major decisions should not be left to them alone, since these choices belong to everyone.
The wisest policy joins expert knowledge with the values and consent of the public.
